entries.availWhy: Rising, hand use, the number of attempts, independent stabilization and the presence of examiner contact are visible. The distinction between grades 1 and 0 depends on how much of the lifting or stabilizing effort the examiner carries, which the image does not show.
entries.missing: Whether the physical help was minimal (grade 1) or moderate to maximal (grade 0), i.e. the share of the lifting or stabilizing effort provided by the examiner.
entries.altSource: examiner's record of the clinical decision
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) and front views of the whole body, the chair with its armrests and the examiner's hands, from sitting until stable standing. Seat-off and every attempt must be captured.
entries.features: sit-to-stand transition; hand/arm push-off (wrist→thigh/armrest); time-to-stable; attempts
entries.compWhy: Visible part: hand use, number of attempts and stability without help

entries.availWhy: Standing time, the number of attempts, sway, touching of supports and any rescue are visible. The need for supervision (grade 3) is judged from visible excessive sway or instability, which is how the ANPT document defines it, not from the examiner's presence alone.
entries.recording: Front or oblique full-body view including the feet and any nearby support, recorded for the full 2 minutes with a visible start and timestamps; the examiner's position relative to the patient should be in frame.
entries.features: unsupported standing duration; trunk sway amplitude
entries.compWhy: Safely vs with supervision is a rater judgement of visible steadiness

entries.availWhy: Sitting duration, folded arms, trunk steadiness and loss of balance are visible, and the need for supervision is judged from visible instability as in item 2. When the item is credited from item 2, the information is contained in the item 2 recording.
entries.recording: Front or side view of the whole seated patient, including the feet, seat and hands, for 2 minutes with timestamps; if the item is credited from item 2, the item 2 recording must be available.
entries.features: seated-balance duration; trunk lean angle
entries.compWhy: Safely vs with supervision is a rater judgement of visible steadiness

entries.availWhy: Hand use, contact of the legs with the chair, the speed and control of the descent and the presence of help are visible. Grade 0 depends only on whether help occurs, not on its amount.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view with the chair, armrests, backs of the legs and the moment of seat contact in frame, at a frame rate sufficient to judge descent speed (at least 25-30 frames per second).
entries.features: sit-down detection; descent velocity/control; hand use
entries.compWhy: Controlled vs uncontrolled descent and degree of hand use are rated

entries.info: assistance or supervision; safety judgement; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Hand use, the transfer itself, supervision indicated by visible instability and the number of persons assisting are visible. Grade 2 can be defined by verbal cueing alone, which silent video does not capture.
entries.missing: Whether verbal cueing was given during the transfer, which by itself separates grade 2 from grades 3-4 when the transfer is otherwise performed safely without help.
entries.altSource: audio recording
entries.recording: Wide full-body view including both seating surfaces and every person near the patient, for both directions; an audio track is required to capture verbal cueing.
entries.features: transfer detection; hand-support use; (helper presence)
entries.compWhy: Minor use of the hands vs clearly needs the hands is a rated degree

entries.availWhy: Eye closure, standing time, sway and any rescue are visible; the need for supervision is judged from visible instability as in item 2.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with the face resolved well enough to confirm eye closure (or an additional face close-up), recorded for at least 10 seconds from eye closure with timestamps.
entries.features: eye-closure confirmation; eyes-closed standing duration; trunk/CoM sway amplitude
entries.compWhy: Safely vs with supervision is a rater judgement of visible steadiness

entries.availWhy: Foot placement, help to attain the position, hold time, sway and instability that warrants supervision are visible. Help with positioning is a grade criterion here and is visible when it occurs.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with both feet clearly visible at floor level, including the positioning phase and 1 minute of standing, with timestamps.
entries.features: feet-together detection (ankle keypoints); hold time; sway
entries.compWhy: Safely vs with supervision is a rater judgement of visible steadiness

entries.availWhy: Reach distance can be read from the image when a ruler or other calibrated reference lies in the plane of the reach; trunk rotation, confidence, loss of balance and external support are visible. The need for supervision is judged from visible instability.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) view perpendicular to the reach, with the ruler or a calibrated scale in the plane of the arm and the feet in frame, from the 90-degree starting position to the return; the camera should be level with the fingertips to limit parallax.
entries.features: forward reach distance in cm/in; foot movement; trunk strategy; loss of balance
entries.compWhy: Reach distances are direct; confident or safe reach vs supervision is rated

entries.availWhy: Success in picking up the object, the remaining distance to it (with a reference in view), balance and help are visible; the need for supervision is judged from visible instability.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view with the object, the feet and the hand at floor level in frame and no furniture hidden behind the legs; a scale next to the object is needed to judge the 2-5 cm distance.
entries.features: squat/bend detection; reach-to-floor; recovery to upright
entries.compWhy: Picking up safely and easily vs with supervision is rated

entries.availWhy: Head and trunk rotation to each side, weight shift, loss of balance and help are visible; the need for supervision is judged from visible instability.
entries.recording: Full-body front view (the examiner's perspective), with an additional overhead or rear view if available, so that rotation and weight shift to both sides can be seen; the feet must be in frame to confirm that they stay in place.
entries.features: head/trunk rotation range bilaterally; weight shift; sway/loss of balance
entries.compWhy: Good vs less weight shift is rated without a threshold

entries.info: assistance or supervision; safety judgement; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Turn time in each direction, steadiness, close supervision indicated by visible instability, and help are visible. Grade 1 can also be assigned for verbal cueing, which silent video does not capture.
entries.missing: Whether verbal cueing was given during the turns, which by itself places a safe but slow turn in grade 1 rather than grade 2.
entries.altSource: audio recording
entries.recording: Full-body front or overhead view with the feet visible for both turns, with timestamps for the start and end of each turn; an audio track is required to capture cueing.
entries.features: 360-degree turn duration per direction; step count; continuity; instability/assist cues
entries.compWhy: Turn time is direct; safely but slowly and close supervision are rated

entries.availWhy: Step count, time and any visible contact are obtainable from the image. Grades 2, 1 and 0 are separated by whether a contact actually assisted the patient and by how much (minimal help versus help to prevent a fall), which the image does not reliably show.
entries.missing: Whether an examiner contact was guarding only or gave assistance (grade 2 versus grade 1), and whether the assistance was minimal or was needed to prevent a fall (grade 1 versus grade 0).
entries.altSource: examiner's record of the clinical decision
entries.recording: Full-body side or oblique view with the step, both feet and the examiner's hands in frame, timestamped from the first foot lift to the eighth touch.
entries.features: alternating foot-on-stool count; total time; stance stability; assistance/hand-use cues
entries.compWhy: Step count and time are direct; independently and safely vs supervision is rated

entries.availWhy: Foot placement relative to the other foot, step width, help with stepping, hold time and loss of balance are visible.
entries.recording: Full-body view plus a floor-level or overhead view of both feet, for up to 30 seconds with timestamps.
entries.features: tandem/semi-tandem foot placement; hold duration; sway/loss of balance
entries.compWhy: Foot placement, holding time and help to step are measurable events

entries.availWhy: Foot lift, hold time, contact of the lifted leg, touch-down and any help are visible.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with both feet visible so that foot-off and touch-down can be detected, with timestamps.
entries.features: single-leg stance time per leg; stance-leg/trunk sway
entries.compWhy: Independent leg lift and holding times

entries.availWhy: Hand use, arm thrusting, the number of attempts, stabilization and the presence of physical assistance are visible; because any physical assistance gives 0, its amount is not needed.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view with the chair, seat contact and both hands in frame from sitting to stable standing; every attempt must be recorded.
entries.features: sit-to-stand; hand push-off; attempts
entries.compWhy: Hand use, number of attempts and assistance are discrete events

entries.availWhy: Heel height, hold time and instability are visible; the reference height is visible when the hand-held comparison rise is also recorded.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) view including the whole body and the feet at floor level, for both attempts and any hand-held comparison rise, with timestamps; a floor-level camera improves heel-height comparison.
entries.features: heel-rise height (ankle/heel keypoint); hold time; sway
entries.compWhy: Heel height relative to the supported trial is measurable; noticeable instability is rated

entries.availWhy: Foot lift, hands on hips, touch-down and hold time on each side are visible.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with both feet and the hands on the hips visible for all four trials, timestamped from foot lift to the end condition (maximum 20 seconds).
entries.features: single-leg stance time per side; sway; hands-off-hips detection
entries.compWhy: Holding time

entries.availWhy: The lean position at release, the release itself, the number of steps and any catch by the examiner are visible. The examiner's sensing of body weight before release standardizes the perturbation but does not define a grade.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view with room in front of the patient, showing the examiner's hands, the lean (shoulders and hips relative to the toes), the release and every step until stable, at a frame rate of at least 25-30 frames per second.
entries.features: forward recovery-step detection; step count
entries.compWhy: Number of recovery steps; fall

entries.availWhy: The lean position at release, the release, the number of backward steps and any catch are visible; the examiner's sensing of body weight standardizes the perturbation but does not define a grade.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view with room behind the patient, showing the examiner's hands, the lean (shoulders and hips relative to the heels), the release and every step until stable, at a frame rate of at least 25-30 frames per second.
entries.features: backward recovery-step detection; count
entries.compWhy: Number of recovery steps; fall

entries.availWhy: The lean of the pelvis over the foot, the release, the number and type of steps and any fall or catch are visible for each side.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) full-body view with room to both sides, showing the examiner's hand on the pelvis, the release and every step until stable, for both sides, at a frame rate of at least 25-30 frames per second.
entries.features: lateral recovery-step detection; count; worse side
entries.compWhy: Number of recovery steps; fall

entries.task: Stance feet together, eyes open, firm [Sensory orientation]
entries.availWhy: Foot position, hands on hips, standing time and loss of the position are visible.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with both feet visible at floor level, recorded for up to 30 seconds with timestamps.
entries.features: feet-together hold time; sway
entries.compWhy: Holding time

entries.task: Stance feet together, eyes closed, foam [Sensory orientation]
entries.availWhy: The foam surface, foot position, eye closure, standing time and loss of the position are visible; help stepping onto the foam belongs to the set-up and does not change the grade.
entries.recording: Full-body front view with the foam and the feet in frame and the face resolved well enough to confirm eye closure, timestamped from eye closure for up to 30 seconds.
entries.features: 30-s eyes-closed foam stance duration; sway; eye-closure and foam-condition confirmation
entries.compWhy: Holding time

entries.availWhy: Standing time, eye closure and body alignment relative to the vertical and to the ramp surface are visible in a sagittal view.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) full-body view perpendicular to the slope with the ramp and a vertical reference in frame, and the face resolved well enough to confirm eye closure, timestamped from eye closure for up to 30 seconds.
entries.features: incline stance duration; trunk alignment relative to gravity/surface; sway; eye-closure confirmation
entries.compWhy: Holding time; trunk alignment with gravity vs with the surface is an angle

entries.availWhy: Speed in each phase (position over time along a marked walkway) and imbalance are visible. The spoken commands are standard instructions; their timing can be marked by a visible signal or audio, and they do not define a grade.
entries.recording: Side view of the whole walkway with distance markers, covering all three speed phases; an audio track or a visible signal is needed to mark the 'fast' and 'slow' commands.
entries.features: gait-speed change magnitude; acceleration/deceleration; imbalance/path deviation
entries.compWhy: Significant change in speed and signs of imbalance are rated without thresholds

entries.task: Walk with horizontal head turns [Dynamic gait]
entries.availWhy: Head orientation, gait speed along a marked walkway, path deviation and imbalance are visible; the spoken direction commands are standard instructions and do not define a grade.
entries.recording: Full-body views along the walkway (side plus front or back) with the head orientation visible and distance markers to estimate speed; audio or a visible signal marking the commands is helpful.
entries.features: horizontal head-turn detection; gait-speed change; path deviation; imbalance
entries.compWhy: Change in gait speed and good balance vs imbalance are rated

entries.availWhy: The step count from the command to a stable stance, the final foot position, turn speed and the listed signs of imbalance are visible; the command is a standard instruction whose moment can be marked by a visible signal or audio.
entries.recording: Overhead or front-oblique full-body view with the feet visible throughout the turn, and an audio track or visible signal marking the 'turn and stop' command so that the step count can start at the command.
entries.features: pivot-turn detection; step count; turn time; imbalance
entries.compWhy: Step count is direct; good balance vs imbalance is rated

entries.availWhy: Clearance, contact with the box, stepping around it, gait speed before and at the obstacle and balance are visible.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) view of the approach, crossing and departure, with the box and the feet at floor level in frame and distance markers along the path to estimate speed.
entries.features: obstacle clearance (foot-box distance); speed change; contact
entries.compWhy: Touching the box is an event; minimal speed change and cautious behaviour are rated

entries.task: Timed Up & Go with dual task [Dynamic gait]
entries.info: time, distance or count; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Both TUG times, the percentage slowing, new imbalance and any stopping of walking are visible. Whether counting slowed, stopped or lost accuracy, and the seated counting baseline, can only be heard.
entries.missing: The seated baseline counting rate and accuracy, the counting rate and accuracy while walking, and whether the patient stopped counting while walking; these separate grade 2 from grade 1 (counting affected) and define one of the grade 0 conditions.
entries.altSource: audio recording
entries.recording: Side view of the whole 3-m course with the chair and the tape line in frame for both TUG trials, with synchronized audio capturing the 'Go' command and the counting from the seated baseline onward.
entries.features: TUG phase times; gait-speed change single vs dual task; (counting from audio)
entries.compWhy: Visible part: walking slows by more than 10% relative to the single-task TUG

entries.availWhy: Walking time over the marked 6 m, lateral deviation relative to the marked lane, device use, gait pattern, imbalance and wall contact are visible when the lane markings are in frame.
entries.recording: Front or rear view along the walkway to read lateral deviation against the lane markings, plus a side view for timing and gait pattern; the start mark, the 6-m mark and both lane edges must be visible throughout.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Normal gait pattern vs mild gait deviations is an overall pattern judgement

entries.availWhy: Speed in each 1.5-m segment, smoothness, lateral deviation, loss of balance, wall contact and catching are visible; the 'go' and 'slow' commands are standard instructions and do not define a grade.
entries.recording: Side view of the whole walkway with markers at each 1.5-m segment for speed, plus a front or rear view against the lane edges; audio or a visible signal marking the commands is helpful.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Gait deviation is an overall pattern judgement

entries.availWhy: Head-turn timing and smoothness, gait velocity, lateral deviation, staggering, stopping and wall contact are visible; cues to remind the patient when to turn the head are documented trial conditions and do not define a grade.
entries.recording: Front or rear view along the walkway with the head orientation and lane edges visible, plus a side view with distance markers for velocity, over the full 6 m.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Path deviation is measured; smoothness and change in gait velocity are rated

entries.availWhy: Head flexion and extension, gait velocity, lateral deviation, staggering, stopping and wall contact are visible; reminder cues are documented trial conditions and do not define a grade.
entries.recording: Side view with distance markers and the head profile visible, plus a front or rear view against the lane edges, over the full 6 m.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Path deviation is measured; smoothness and change in gait velocity are rated

entries.info: assistance or supervision; safety judgement; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Turn time, catch steps, imbalance and assistance are visible. Grade 1 can be assigned for verbal cueing alone, which silent video does not capture.
entries.missing: Whether the patient needed verbal cueing to complete the turn and stop, which by itself can place an otherwise grade 2 performance in grade 1.
entries.altSource: audio recording
entries.recording: Overhead or front-oblique full-body view with the feet visible through the turn and stop, a visible signal or audio marking the command for timing, and an audio track to capture cueing.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Pivot time is direct; mild imbalance and safety of the turn are rated

entries.info: assistance or supervision; time, distance or count
entries.availWhy: Obstacle height (one or two boxes), clearance, gait speed, step adjustment, imbalance and assistance are visible. The verbal cue mentioned under grade 1 is optional and does not define the grade by itself, because grade 1 requires the visible slowing and step adjustment.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) view of the approach, crossing and departure with the obstacle and the feet at floor level in frame and distance markers for speed; the obstacle height (one or two boxes) must be visible or labelled.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Obstacle height is fixed; change in speed and evidence of imbalance are rated

entries.task: Gait with narrow base of support
entries.availWhy: Heel-to-toe foot placement, the number of steps in a straight line, arm position, staggering and assistance are visible.
entries.recording: Side and front (or overhead) views of the full 3.6-m path with the feet at floor level and the floor line in frame, so that each heel-to-toe step can be counted.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Number of heel-to-toe steps without staggering

entries.availWhy: Eye closure, walking time, lateral deviation, device use, gait pattern, imbalance and a failure to attempt are visible.
entries.recording: Front or rear view along the walkway against the lane edges plus a side view for timing, with the face resolved well enough to confirm that the eyes stay closed over the full 6 m.
entries.features: eyes-closed walking time; lateral deviation; gait quality; eye-closure confirmation
entries.compWhy: Normal gait pattern vs mild gait deviations is an overall pattern judgement

entries.availWhy: Distance, speed, gait pattern, imbalance, lateral deviation, device use and a failure to attempt are visible.
entries.recording: Front or rear view along the walkway against the lane edges plus a side view with distance markers, covering the full 6 m of backward walking.
entries.features: time over 6 m; lateral deviation (cm) from lane centre (pelvis/ankle trajectory); turn time/steps; foot clearance; stair pattern
entries.compWhy: Normal gait pattern vs mild gait deviations is an overall pattern judgement

entries.availWhy: Foot pattern, rail use, instability, failure and rescue are visible, so the grade-0 condition 'cannot do safely' is obtainable when instability, failure or rescue is recorded. If the task was not attempted for a reason that is not recorded, the video is incomplete for this item.
entries.recording: Side view of the entire staircase showing both rails and the patient's feet and hands during ascent, turn and descent.
entries.features: stair ascent/descent pattern; alternating vs step-to; rail use; imbalance/safety cues
entries.compWhy: Rail use and foot placement pattern

entries.availWhy: Sitting duration, arm support and falling are visible.
entries.recording: Front view of the whole seated patient including the hands, both feet and the table edge, camera at trunk height, timestamped for at least 10 seconds per attempt, with all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted in the test metadata.
entries.features: unsupported-sit duration; trunk lean angle; arm-support detection
entries.compWhy: Holding time; arm support; fall

entries.task: Static: Therapist crosses unaffected leg over hemiplegic leg
entries.availWhy: The therapist's passive leg crossing (part of the set-up), sitting time, arm support and falling are visible.
entries.recording: Front view of the whole seated patient including the hands, both feet and the table edge, camera at trunk height, timestamped for at least 10 seconds per attempt, with all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted in the test metadata. The therapist's leg-crossing action must also be in frame.
entries.features: post-cross sit duration; trunk lean; (therapist action)
entries.compWhy: Holding time; arm support; fall

entries.task: Static: Patient crosses unaffected leg over hemiplegic leg
entries.availWhy: Leg crossing, hand assistance, arm support on the surface and falling are visible; backward trunk displacement of more than 10 cm is measurable with a scale in the sagittal plane.
entries.recording: Side (sagittal) view of the trunk, pelvis, legs and hands with a scale or markers at trunk height to measure a 10-cm backward displacement, the table surface visible, and a front view to confirm hand use; all attempts recorded.
entries.features: leg-crossing detection; backward trunk displacement (cm, needs scale); hand-support use
entries.compWhy: Trunk displacement threshold (10 cm), hand assistance and arm support

entries.task: Touch bed with hemiplegic elbow (shorten hemiplegic/lengthen unaffected side) & return
entries.availWhy: Elbow contact with the surface, active movement without help, upper-extremity support and falling are visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: lateral trunk flexion angle; elbow-to-surface contact; support use
entries.compWhy: Elbow contact with the bed; arm support; fall

entries.availWhy: Shortening and lengthening of the two trunk sides are visible movement-quality features; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. Both lateral trunk contours must be unobstructed.
entries.features: lateral-flexion symmetry; hemiplegic-side shortening vs lengthening
entries.compWhy: Appropriate shortening and lengthening of the trunk sides is rated without a threshold

entries.availWhy: Arm use, hip abduction, the elbow contact point relative to the proximal half of the femur, knee flexion and foot sliding are all visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. A mark at the mid-point of the femur helps to judge the hip-flexion criterion, and the feet must remain in frame to detect sliding.
entries.features: compensation detection (arm use, hip abduction/flexion, foot slide)
entries.compWhy: Five listed compensation strategies need detection thresholds

entries.task: Touch bed with unaffected elbow (shorten unaffected/lengthen hemiplegic) & return
entries.availWhy: Elbow contact with the surface, active movement without help, upper-extremity support and falling are visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: lateral flexion angle (unaffected side); elbow contact; support
entries.compWhy: Elbow contact with the bed; arm support; fall

entries.availWhy: Shortening and lengthening of the two trunk sides are visible movement-quality features; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. Both lateral trunk contours must be unobstructed.
entries.features: lateral-flexion symmetry
entries.compWhy: Appropriate shortening and lengthening of the trunk sides is rated without a threshold

entries.availWhy: Arm use, hip abduction, the elbow contact point relative to the proximal half of the femur, knee flexion and foot sliding are all visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient from head to feet including both elbows, both hands, the pelvis, thighs and feet and the table surface, camera at trunk height and perpendicular to the frontal plane; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. A mark at the mid-point of the femur helps to judge the hip-flexion criterion, and the feet must remain in frame to detect sliding.
entries.features: compensation detection
entries.compWhy: Five listed compensation strategies need detection thresholds

entries.task: Lift pelvis, hemiplegic side (shorten hemiplegic/lengthen unaffected) & return
entries.availWhy: Pelvic lift and the shortening and lengthening of the two trunk sides are visible movement-quality features; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient including the trunk, pelvis, both hands and both feet at floor level (heel contact visible), camera at pelvis height; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: pelvis-hike detection; hemiplegic-side shortening
entries.compWhy: Appropriate shortening and lengthening of the trunk sides is rated without a threshold

entries.availWhy: Use of the arm or arms and loss of heel contact on the ipsilateral side are visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient including the trunk, pelvis, both hands and both feet at floor level (heel contact visible), camera at pelvis height; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. Both heels must be visible at floor level.
entries.features: foot heel-contact loss; arm push detection
entries.compWhy: Upper-extremity use or heel lift-off are discrete events

entries.task: Lift pelvis, unaffected side (shorten unaffected/lengthen hemiplegic) & return
entries.availWhy: Pelvic lift and the shortening and lengthening of the two trunk sides are visible movement-quality features; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient including the trunk, pelvis, both hands and both feet at floor level (heel contact visible), camera at pelvis height; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: pelvis-hike detection (unaffected side)
entries.compWhy: Appropriate shortening and lengthening of the trunk sides is rated without a threshold

entries.availWhy: Use of the arm or arms and loss of heel contact on the ipsilateral side are visible.
entries.recording: Front (frontal-plane) view of the seated patient including the trunk, pelvis, both hands and both feet at floor level (heel contact visible), camera at pelvis height; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted. Both heels must be visible at floor level.
entries.features: foot heel-contact loss; arm push
entries.compWhy: Upper-extremity use or heel lift-off are discrete events

entries.task: Coordination: Rotate upper trunk 6× (shoulders, head fixated)
entries.availWhy: The number of forward movements of each side, the order of movement, fixation of the head and the symmetry of rotation are visible; observer judgement of visible symmetry is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front view and, if possible, an overhead view of the seated patient with both shoulders and the head visible, so that each forward shoulder movement, the order of movement and head fixation can be judged; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: upper-trunk rotation amplitude L/R; symmetry
entries.compWhy: Symmetrical vs asymmetrical rotation has no threshold

entries.availWhy: Rotation symmetry and the time to complete the 6 rotations are visible with a timed recording.
entries.recording: Front and, if possible, overhead view of both shoulders and the head, timestamped from the first movement to the sixth rotation to verify the 6-second limit.
entries.features: rotation symmetry within 6 s; rotation rate
entries.compWhy: Symmetry is rated; the 6-s limit is direct

entries.task: Coordination: Rotate lower trunk 6× (knees, upper trunk fixated)
entries.availWhy: The number of forward movements of each side, the order of movement, fixation of the upper trunk and the symmetry of rotation are visible; observer judgement of visible symmetry is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Front view of the seated patient with both knees, the pelvis and the upper trunk visible (camera at knee to pelvis height, overhead view if possible), so that each forward knee movement, the order of movement and upper-trunk fixation can be judged; all attempts recorded and the hemiplegic side noted.
entries.features: lower-trunk rotation amplitude L/R; symmetry
entries.compWhy: Symmetrical vs asymmetrical rotation has no threshold

entries.availWhy: Rotation symmetry and the time to complete the 6 rotations are visible with a timed recording.
entries.recording: Front view of both knees, the pelvis and the upper trunk, timestamped from the first movement to the sixth rotation to verify the 6-second limit.
entries.features: lower-trunk rotation symmetry within 6 s
entries.compWhy: Symmetry is rated; the 6-s limit is direct

entries.task: Comfortable & fast gait speed over middle 6 m of a 10 m path (2 m accel + 6 m timed + 2 m decel)
entries.availWhy: Both timing events (leading foot crossing the 2-m and 8-m planes) and the marked 6-m distance are visible, so speed for each trial can be computed from the image. Hands-on help that moves a limb or propels the patient, which sets the score to 0, is visible; the separately documented 7-point assistance level is not part of the speed score.

entries.recording: Frontal and lateral (or a single oblique) whole-body view of the patient, feet included, for the whole manoeuvre, with the face visible to confirm eye closure.
entries.features: eye-closure confirmation; standing steadiness/sway; balance loss
entries.compWhy: Steady vs unsteady

entries.availWhy: Step continuity and grabbing or staggering during the turn are visible. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Frontal and lateral (or a single oblique) whole-body view of the patient, feet included, for the whole manoeuvre, including the whole turn with the feet visible.
entries.features: task detection; relevant kinematic measure per criterion
entries.compWhy: Step continuity and steadiness are rated

entries.availWhy: Smoothness, arm use and an uncontrolled drop into the chair are visible. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Frontal and lateral (or a single oblique) whole-body view of the patient, feet included, for the whole manoeuvre, with both hands and the chair seat in frame.
entries.features: task detection; relevant kinematic measure per criterion
entries.compWhy: Smooth motion and misjudged distance are rated

entries.availWhy: Hesitation and false starts after the start command are visible when the command is marked. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout, and the start command marked by audio or a visible signal.
entries.features: task detection; relevant kinematic measure per criterion
entries.compWhy: Hesitancy is rated

entries.availWhy: Foot passage relative to the stance foot and foot clearance are visible in a low sagittal view of both legs. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path at floor level (so that the clearance of each foot is visible) and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout.
entries.features: step length L/R; foot clearance (toe-floor distance) each foot
entries.compWhy: Swing foot passes the stance foot; foot clears the floor

entries.availWhy: Right and left step lengths are visible and can be estimated or measured. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout, with a floor reference of known length in the sagittal view.
entries.features: step-length symmetry ratio
entries.compWhy: Step lengths appear equal; no threshold

entries.availWhy: Stops and pauses between steps are visible. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout.
entries.features: task detection; relevant kinematic measure per criterion
entries.compWhy: Step continuity is rated

entries.availWhy: Lateral excursion of the foot against a floor reference and use of a walking aid are visible. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout, with floor tiles or tape lines of known width visible over at least 10 ft (3 m).
entries.features: pelvis-trajectory lateral deviation
entries.compWhy: Mild, moderate or marked path deviation

entries.availWhy: Trunk sway, knee and back flexion, arm position and walking-aid use are visible. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path, with the feet in frame throughout, with the trunk and both arms in frame.
entries.features: trunk sway amplitude; arm-abduction angle; knee/back flexion
entries.compWhy: Sway, knee or back flexion and arm spreading are rated

entries.availWhy: Heel separation during walking is visible in a frontal view. All grade-defining information is visible; observer judgement of visible movement quality is allowed for Full.
entries.recording: Whole-body views of the walk over the 15-ft walkway in both directions: a sagittal view perpendicular to the path and a frontal view along the path at foot level, with the feet in frame throughout.
entries.features: inter-ankle distance during gait
entries.compWhy: Heels almost touching vs apart; no threshold

entries.task: Distance walked in 2 minutes, fastest safe pace
entries.availWhy: Elapsed time, the distance covered against a marked course, rests and use of an assistive device are visible; the distance is obtainable when the course length or markers are in frame. Rest time counts within the 2 minutes.
entries.recording: A wide or tracking view covering the whole course with distance markers at known intervals and the turning points, a continuous 2-minute recording with a synchronized start signal or on-screen clock, and the stopping point visible relative to the nearest marker; the assistive device in frame.
entries.features: cumulative distance over 2 min; speed decay; rest detection; gait speed
entries.compWhy: Distance in 2 min

entries.availWhy: Foot positions, hold times, stepping out of position, grabbing the tester and the moment the tester lets go are all visible; hold times are obtainable with a synchronized timer.
entries.recording: Whole-body view with a close or low frontal view of the feet to verify the side-by-side, semi-tandem and tandem positions, the tester's hands visible at release, and a synchronized timer or time stamp from 'Ready, begin' to stop.
entries.features: stance-hold times; 4 m gait speed; 5× rise time; arm-fold compliance
entries.compWhy: Holding times

entries.task: Gait speed (4 m walk, 2 trials, faster used)
entries.availWhy: Start of walking, the moment one foot fully crosses the end line, the course length and use of a walking aid are visible; time over the marked course is obtainable from the recording.
entries.recording: Sagittal whole-body view of the entire course with the start and end lines and the feet visible (ideally a camera perpendicular to the end line, or two views), with a synchronized timer; both trials recorded.
entries.features: stance-hold times; 4 m gait speed; 5× rise time; arm-fold compliance
entries.compWhy: Walk-time bands

entries.availWhy: Arm position, full standing at each rise, the number of rises and the time from the start command to the fifth full stand are visible with a synchronized timer.
entries.recording: Sagittal whole-body view of the chair and the participant with the arms, hips and knees visible throughout, the start command marked by audio or a visible signal, and a synchronized timer until the fifth full stand.
entries.features: stance-hold times; 4 m gait speed; 5× rise time; arm-fold compliance
entries.compWhy: Chair-stand time bands

entries.task: Walk fastest across 1×5 m field kicking blocks out of 5 circles
entries.availWhy: Elapsed time, the walking path, the foot used, block displacement out of each circle and use of an assistive device are visible with a synchronized timer.
entries.recording: An overhead or high oblique wide view covering the whole 1 x 5 m field, with all circles and blocks visible throughout and block positions relative to the circle edges resolvable at the end of each run; synchronized timing from the first foot lift; all four runs recorded.
entries.features: completion time; path; foot-to-block kicking detection; step count
entries.compWhy: Run time

entries.task: Section 1: Sitting (Levels 1-3: supported sitting / static sitting / dynamic sitting)
entries.availWhy: Sitting duration, arm support, the number and range of arm lifts, hand touch-down and the reach distance against a ruler in frame are all visible. The tester standing beside the patient does not by itself change the grade; actual tester support or assistance, which fails a level, is visible.
entries.recording: Frontal-oblique view of the whole seated patient including the feet, both hands, the seat and the tester; for level 3, a side view perpendicular to the ruler with its graduations legible; a synchronized timer for the 30 s and 15 s periods; every attempt recorded.
entries.features: level-task detection (hold times, reach distance, step performance); sway
entries.compWhy: Holding time, arm-lift counts, reach distance and arm support

entries.task: Section 2: Standing (static & dynamic standing balance levels)
entries.availWhy: Standing duration, holding on, the number and range of arm lifts, touch-down and the reach distance against a ruler in frame are all visible. The tester standing beside the patient does not by itself change the grade; actual tester support or assistance, which fails a level, is visible.
entries.recording: Frontal-oblique whole-body view including the feet, both hands, any support furniture and the tester; for level 6, a side view perpendicular to the ruler with legible graduations and the heels visible; a synchronized timer for the 30 s and 15 s periods; every attempt recorded.
entries.features: level-task detection (hold times, reach distance, step performance); sway
entries.compWhy: Holding time, arm-lift counts, reach distance and arm support

entries.availWhy: Step-standing duration, 5 m walking times against a marked walkway, walking-aid use, contact with the front bar and rear stool, taps and step-ups on a block, arm support and physical support from the tester are all visible. The tester standing beside the patient does not by itself change the grade; actual tester support or assistance, which fails a level, is visible.
entries.recording: Whole-body views including both feet: for levels 8 and 10 a sagittal view of the 5 m walkway with the start and finish lines; for level 9 a lateral view showing contact with the front bar and the rear stool; for levels 11 and 12 a lateral view of the block showing whole-foot placement; the tester in frame and a synchronized timer for the 30 s and 15 s periods and walk times; every attempt recorded.
entries.features: level-task detection (hold times, reach distance, step performance); sway
entries.compWhy: Holding time, walking time, weight-transfer counts and support

entries.availWhy: The grade depends on whether the transfer is completed and on how many people physically help, both of which are visible when the whole manoeuvre and every helper are in frame.
entries.recording: Lateral view of the bed showing the patient's whole body and every person near the bed from the supine start until stable sitting on the bed edge; add an oblique second view if a helper may hide the patient.
entries.features: transfer completion; assistance
entries.compWhy: Number of helpers

entries.availWhy: Completion of the manoeuvre and the number of people physically helping are visible when the patient and all helpers are recorded throughout.
entries.recording: Lateral view of the bed with the patient's whole body and all helpers in frame from sitting on the bed edge until the supine position is reached; add an oblique second view if a helper may hide the patient.
entries.features: transfer completion; assistance
entries.compWhy: Number of helpers

entries.info: assistance or supervision; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Rise time, physical help and the number of helpers are visible, but grade 1 explicitly includes verbal help from one person; a patient who stands only after spoken prompting would be misread as independent (grade 2 or 3) on a silent video.
entries.missing: Whether one person helped verbally (instructions, prompting or encouragement during the rise), which separates grade 1 from grades 2-3 when no physical help is given.
entries.altSource: audio recording
entries.recording: Lateral view of the chair and the whole body including feet and hands, with any helper in frame; time-stamped video for the 3-second threshold; synchronized audio track to capture verbal help.
entries.features: transfer completion; assistance
entries.compWhy: Visible part: time and occurrence of physical help

entries.availWhy: Upper-limb steadying, physical support from a person and the reach itself are visible. The decided code is Partial because grade 2 ('needs help to reach') is not operationally defined: the help may be verbal or may reflect the examiner's judgement that reaching needed help, which leaves no visible trace.
entries.missing: Whether help that defines grade 2 was given verbally or was judged necessary without visible contact; the examiner's decision separating grade 2 from grade 3 when no visible support occurs.
entries.altSource: audio recording; examiner's record of the clinical decision
entries.recording: Frontal-oblique view of the whole body including both hands, any nearby support surface and any helper; the reach must be recorded with the arm and feet in frame; synchronized audio for verbal help.
entries.features: standing + reach within arm's length; support use
entries.compWhy: Visible part: support use and reach

entries.availWhy: Aid type, gait steadiness, turning and physical assistance are visible. Grade 0 also covers 'constant supervision', a judgement of safety need: an examiner walking alongside is visible, but whether supervision is required rather than precautionary, and where erratic turning becomes a need for supervision, cannot be read from one recorded walk.
entries.missing: Whether constant supervision is required (grade 0) as opposed to mobile but erratic or unsafe (grade 1) when no physical assistance occurs; the examiner's safety judgement.
entries.altSource: examiner's record of the clinical decision
entries.recording: Wide sagittal or frontal-oblique view covering the whole walkway and the turn, whole body including feet and the walking aid, and every accompanying person in frame.
entries.features: gait independence/aid; erratic turning
entries.compWhy: Visible part: erratic or unsafe walking is rated

entries.availWhy: Walking time over a marked 6-m distance can be obtained from time-stamped video when the start and finish lines are visible.
entries.recording: Wide sagittal view of a 6-m course with start and finish lines marked on the floor and both in frame, whole body including feet visible; time-stamped video from before the start to after the finish.
entries.features: 6 m walk time
entries.compWhy: Walk time

entries.availWhy: Reach distance is a length that can be read from video when a calibrated reference (metre stick) is in frame along the reach path; stepping or loss of balance is visible.
entries.recording: Sagittal view perpendicular to the reach direction with the camera at shoulder height, the metre stick on the wall in frame along the reach path, and the whole body including the feet visible from start to maximal reach.
entries.features: functional reach distance in cm; foot movement; balance loss
entries.compWhy: Reach distance

entries.task: 13 high-level balance/mobility tasks (e.g. unilateral stance, tandem walking, 360° turns, lateral foot scooting, hopping, running with controlled stop, walking & looking, descending stairs, crouch-and-walk)
entries.availWhy: All grade criteria are times, counts of steps, pivots, hops and cycles, distances on a marked track, foot placement on the line, path deviation, protective steps, support use and observer-judged coordination, which are visible in a whole-body recording of each task with the track marks in frame.
entries.recording: Wide sagittal-oblique view of the whole 8-m track with the 1-, 2-, 4-, 6- and 8-m marks and the target in frame and the whole body including feet visible, plus a separate view of the staircase; time-stamped video for all timed tasks. A head/face view (second camera) is needed to judge visual fixation in tasks 8 and 11, and an audio track to time the examiner's 'Change!' cue in task 7.
entries.features: task segmentation; time/steps; spatiotemporal gait params; sway/control during dynamic tasks
entries.compWhy: Times and steps are direct; coordinated, controlled and excessive equilibrium reactions are rated

entries.task: 14 seated-balance tasks (static sitting, anterior/posterior/lateral nudges, eyes closed, lateral & forward reach, pick object from floor, scooting, etc.)
entries.info: assistance or supervision; time, distance or count; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: Completion, hand use for support, physical help, nudges and balance reactions, 30-s holds and scoot distances are visible. Grade 3 rests on verbal cues (audio) and on 'increased time' judged against normal, and grade 1 versus 0 rests on the share of the effort provided by the therapist (physical assistance versus complete assistance), which cannot be read from the image.
entries.missing: Whether verbal cues were given (grade 3 versus 4, and the cue-dependent rules); the therapist's share of effort separating grade 1 (minimal to maximal assistance) from grade 0 (complete assistance or unable); the examiner's judgement that a performance was unsafe but made safe by cueing.
entries.altSource: audio recording; examiner's record of the clinical decision
entries.recording: Frontal plus lateral (or oblique) view of the seated patient with the whole trunk, both hands, thighs, feet, bed surface and the examiner's hands in frame (nudges and assistance must be visible); tape measure or floor markings visible for scooting; time-stamped video and synchronized audio for cues.
entries.features: trunk lean/sway; reach excursion; reactive-recovery detection; scooting detection
entries.compWhy: Visible part: normal speed and safety and tentative or slow performance are rated

entries.task: Manual ability questionnaire (perceived difficulty of bimanual ADL tasks)
entries.availWhy: Patient-reported entry: the score is the patient's own rating of difficulty, which does not come from visible performance even if activities were filmed; the information is obtained by interview or questionnaire.
entries.missing: All 23 self-ratings (easy, difficult, impossible) and the not-applicable responses.
entries.altSource: patient report (interview or questionnaire)
entries.recording: Not applicable: no visible information is scored; the questionnaire is completed by interview or on paper (an audio recording of the interview may serve as documentation).
entries.features: perceived manual ability — not observable
entries.compWhy: Self-report; no visible score-defining content

entries.task: 5 functional UL tasks (stabilise ruler & draw line; lift 12 mm cylinder; lift & drink half-full glass; clip clothes-peg on dowel; comb hair)
entries.availWhy: Every pass criterion is a visible object event (ruler slipping, object dropped, water spilled, dowel falling, regions of the head reached), so the whole score can be obtained from an adequate recording.
entries.recording: Frontal-oblique view of the table, the upper body and both hands, including the head for task 5; a hand close-up or second camera on the grasped objects for tasks 2-4; record each task from hands-in-lap to replacement of the object.
entries.features: task completion detection per item; reach-grasp-manipulate; success/failure of object handling
entries.compWhy: Task success: completion without dropping or spilling

entries.task: 7 timed subtests (writing, card turning, small common objects, simulated feeding, stacking checkers, lifting large light cans, lifting large heavy cans)
entries.availWhy: Each score is the elapsed time between the start signal and a visible end event (pen lift, card turned, object in can, checker contact, can released), which can be measured from time-stamped video when the start signal is captured and the hand and objects are in close view.
entries.recording: Overhead or front-oblique close-up of the desk, the working hand and all objects; the start signal must be identifiable (visible card flip or synchronized audio of 'Go'); time-stamped video at a standard frame rate, each hand recorded in full.
entries.features: task timing if close-up available; most subtests are fine manipulation — not whole-body observable
entries.compWhy: Subtest times

entries.task: FE — Forward elevation of upper extremity (arm motion)
entries.availWhy: The grade is the peak shoulder flexion angle, with tolerances for elbow flexion and abduction, all of which are visible kinematic quantities in a sagittal view.
entries.recording: Sagittal view of the affected side with the camera at shoulder height and perpendicular to the plane of motion, trunk, shoulder, elbow and wrist in frame (landmark markers or a goniometric reference recommended); a frontal view to check abduction; record through the peak of the movement.
entries.features: peak shoulder-flexion angle; elbow-extension maintenance; abduction deviation
entries.compWhy: Shoulder flexion angle bands

entries.task: LE — Lateral elevation of upper extremity (arm motion)
entries.availWhy: The grade is the peak shoulder abduction angle with tolerances for elbow and shoulder flexion, all visible in a frontal view.
entries.recording: Frontal (or posterior) view at shoulder height, perpendicular to the plane of abduction, with trunk, shoulder, elbow and wrist of the affected side in frame; a lateral view to check flexion; record through the peak.
entries.features: peak shoulder-abduction angle; elbow-extension maintenance; flexion deviation
entries.compWhy: Shoulder abduction angle bands

entries.task: PO — Touch the occiput with the palm (arm motion)
entries.availWhy: Hand height relative to the xiphisternum, contact with the head, palm placement and the position of the MP joints relative to the occipital midline are visible.
entries.recording: Lateral plus posterior-oblique view of the head, trunk and affected upper limb so that hand contact and the MP joints relative to the occipital midline are visible; record from rest to maximal reach.
entries.features: hand-target proximity (xiphoid→temple→occiput→midline); palm-contact detection
entries.compWhy: Hand position targets

entries.task: PD — Touch the dorsum (back) with the palm (arm motion)
entries.availWhy: Hand position behind the body (buttock, spinal midline, beyond the midline) and palm contact are visible from behind.
entries.recording: Posterior view of the trunk with the spine (midline) and both buttocks visible, plus a lateral view of the affected side; record from rest to maximal reach.
entries.features: hand-target proximity (buttock→dorsum midline→beyond); palm-contact detection
entries.compWhy: Hand position targets

entries.task: GR — Grasp (manipulative: grasp & release of a rubber ball)
entries.availWhy: Holding the ball while the forearm is lifted, release and drop, and whether the grasp or forearm is assisted by the examiner are visible events; the examiner's support is part of the standardized procedure.
entries.recording: Close-up front-oblique view of the affected hand, forearm, ball and table surface, with the examiner's hands in frame; record from grasp to drop.
entries.features: grasp-onset detection; sustained-hold during lift; release/drop event; assistance flag
entries.compWhy: Grasp, hold and release events

entries.task: PI — Pinch (manipulative: pick up pencil / coin / needle)
entries.availWhy: Pinching and lifting each object from the table is a visible event when the fingertips and objects are in close view.
entries.recording: Close-up overhead or oblique view of the affected fingertips and the three objects on the table; record each lift until the object clears the table.
entries.features: pinch-grasp detection; successful lift of pencil/coin/needle; pinch type
entries.compWhy: Object picked up

entries.task: CC — Carry a cube (arm & hand activity, timed)
entries.availWhy: The count of cubes carried beyond the board and released within 5 s is obtainable from time-stamped video with the board and cubes in view.
entries.recording: Overhead or front-oblique view of the table, board, cubes and affected hand; the start signal must be identifiable and the video time-stamped to delimit the 5-s window.
entries.features: count of completed cube transfers in 5 s; cycle-time; drop/miss detection
entries.compWhy: Cube count in 5 s

entries.task: PP — Peg-board (arm & hand activity, timed fine dexterity)
entries.availWhy: The number of pegs correctly seated in the holes within 30 s can be counted from time-stamped close-up video.
entries.recording: Close-up overhead view of the peg-board, saucer and affected hand with every hole visible; identifiable start signal and time-stamped video for the 30-s window.
entries.features: count of pegs correctly inserted in 30 s; insertion-cycle time; drop detection
entries.compWhy: Peg count

entries.task: 10 hierarchical UL capacity tasks (proximal support → reach → grasp/manipulate → fine tasks)
entries.availWhy: Each criterion is a visible event or quantity (forearm not shifting, magazine held 10 s, elbow extension of at least 160 degrees, quarter turn of the marked lid, no spilling, ball grasped, combing strokes, four buttons within 60 s, lines not touched, coins placed); untested tasks are scored by rule from the visible results.
entries.recording: Front-oblique view of the table, trunk and both upper limbs, with hand close-ups for tasks 4, 8, 9 and 10, a lateral view of the elbow for task 3 and the ball position for task 6; time-stamped video for tasks 2 and 8; photograph the completed sheet of task 9.
entries.features: task completion detection per item; reach/support/grasp; proximal tasks whole-body-observable, distal need close-up
entries.compWhy: Task success with specified angles and object conditions

entries.task: Sum of MRC grades for shoulder abduction + finger extension (PREP2 component)
entries.availWhy: Active range against or without gravity (the boundary between grades 2 and 3) is visible, but grades 4 and 5 are defined by the resistance the examiner applies and feels, and grade 1 includes palpable activity, so the video gives only part of the score-defining information.
entries.missing: Grades 3 versus 4 versus 5 for each movement (presence and magnitude of tolerated resistance); grade 1 versus 0 when a contraction is palpable but not visible.
entries.altSource: manual examination (tone, reflex or resistance); force measurement (dynamometer or force sensor)
entries.recording: Frontal view of the patient sitting upright (in bed or chair) showing the paretic shoulder, arm and trunk for abduction range, and a lateral close-up of the forearm, wrist and fingers for finger extension, with the examiner's hands in frame.
entries.features: active shoulder-abduction & finger-extension ROM partly visible; strength-vs-resistance grading not observable
entries.compWhy: Visible part: range against gravity

entries.task: Motor function items (knee-mouth, finger-function, hip-flexion, knee-extension, foot-pat)
entries.availWhy: Grades are defined by visible movement extent and by observer-judged clumsiness relative to the unaffected side, which is allowed for Full; the seated test can be scored from an adequate recording.
entries.recording: Frontal view of the seated patient with the whole body in frame plus a lateral view of the affected side; close-up of the affected hand for the finger test; feet and floor visible for the hip, knee and foot-pat tests; record the unaffected side for comparison, at a frame rate sufficient for tapping.
entries.features: active movement grading from keypoints (motor & trunk items)
entries.compWhy: As smooth as the unaffected side vs mild, moderate or marked clumsiness

entries.task: Muscle tone, deep tendon reflex and range-of-motion items
entries.info: kinematics or movement quality; applied force or touch; tone or reflex
entries.availWhy: Passive joint angles for the two range-of-motion items are visible with a goniometric view, and a tendon tap and visible clonus can be filmed, but the tone grades rest on the resistance the examiner feels during passive movement and the reflex grades on the examiner's tapping and graded judgement of briskness, so only part of the slice is video-obtainable.
entries.missing: All muscle tone grades (resistance felt during passive elbow and knee movement, including hypotonia); reflex grade distinctions (slightly, moderately or markedly increased, nearly absent) that depend on tap force and comparison with the unaffected side; the end point of passive range set by the examiner's force.
entries.altSource: manual examination (tone, reflex or resistance)
entries.recording: For range of motion, a view perpendicular to the plane of motion (frontal for shoulder abduction, sagittal for ankle dorsiflexion) with joint landmarks or a goniometer in frame; for reflexes, a close-up of the tapped tendon and limb response with the examiner's hands visible.
entries.features: tone/reflex/sensation/neglect/aphasia — not video-observable
entries.compWhy: Visible part: passive range-of-motion angles

entries.info: kinematics or movement quality; applied force or touch; verbal cue or response
entries.availWhy: The sit-up from 45 degrees of recline, the trunk tilt and its correction, and the examiner's hand on the sternum are visible. The abdominal-muscle grades are separated by how much resistance the examiner applies at the sternum (none, mild, strong), and verticality grade 2 by whether the patient corrects the tilt after a verbal reminder; neither is visible.
entries.missing: The magnitude of the sternal resistance that separates abdominal-muscle grades 1, 2 and 3, and whether a verbal reminder was given before the tilt was corrected (verticality grade 2 versus 3).
entries.altSource: manual examination (tone, reflex or resistance); audio recording
entries.recording: Frontal view of the seated patient with head, trunk and pelvis in frame and a vertical reference in the background for verticality; lateral view of the reclined chair, trunk angle and the examiner's hand on the sternum for the abdominal test; synchronized audio for instructions.
entries.features: active movement grading from keypoints (motor & trunk items)
entries.compWhy: Visible part: lateral tilt of 15 degrees and its correction

entries.task: Sum of tendon jerk + resistance to passive ankle dorsiflexion + ankle clonus
entries.info: applied force or touch; tone or reflex
entries.availWhy: None: the tendon jerk grade, the resistance felt during passive stretch and the elicitation of clonus are produced and read through the examiner's hammer and hands; clonus beats may be seen on film, but the composite score does not come from visible performance.
entries.missing: All component grades: tendon jerk briskness relative to normal (0-4), resistance to passive dorsiflexion (0-8), and clonus elicitation by the examiner's rapid stretch (1-4).
entries.altSource: manual examination (tone, reflex or resistance); force measurement (dynamometer or force sensor)
entries.recording: Not required for scoring; if filmed for documentation, a lateral close-up of the lower leg, ankle and foot with the examiner's hands visible allows clonus beats to be counted.
entries.features: passive tone, tendon reflex, clonus — not video-observable
entries.compWhy: Reflexes and tone; no visible score-defining content

entries.availWhy: Patient-reported entry: the score is the patient's own confidence rating, which is not a visible performance; it is obtained by interview or questionnaire.
entries.missing: All 10 confidence ratings.
entries.altSource: patient report (interview or questionnaire)
entries.recording: Not applicable: no visible information is scored; the questionnaire is completed on paper or by interview.
entries.features: self-reported fall confidence — not observable
entries.compWhy: Self-report; no visible score-defining content

entries.task: Manual muscle strength grade 0-5 (per muscle; MRC sum score = 6 muscles bilaterally, 0-60)
entries.availWhy: Movement with and against gravity (grades 2 and 3) is visible, but grades 4 and 5 are defined by resistance applied and felt by the examiner, and a trace contraction (grade 1) may be detected by palpation rather than seen.
entries.missing: Grades 3 versus 4 versus 5 (presence and magnitude of tolerated resistance); grade 1 versus 0 when a contraction is palpated but not visible.
entries.altSource: manual examination (tone, reflex or resistance); force measurement (dynamometer or force sensor)
entries.recording: View perpendicular to the plane of the tested movement with the whole segment and adjacent joints in frame and the examiner's hands visible; close-up over the muscle belly for trace contractions.
entries.features: visible contraction and movement against gravity (grades 0-3); resistance grades not observable
entries.compWhy: Visible part: movement against gravity, range and visible contraction

entries.task: Symmetry of spontaneous posture (B: tilt toward paretic side, sitting & standing)
entries.availWhy: The tilt of the body axis, its severity and falling are visible in a whole-body frontal view; grading mild versus severe tilt is an observer judgement of visible posture.
entries.recording: Frontal (or posterior) whole-body view in sitting and in standing with a vertical reference (door frame or plumb line) and the bed and floor in frame, the paretic side annotated and any helper visible.
entries.features: body-tilt angle toward paretic side; spontaneous posture symmetry
entries.compWhy: Severe vs mild tilt is rated; falling is an event

entries.task: Use of nonparetic extremities for abduction/extension (push-off) (sitting & standing)
